Appendix C Runtime-Trace and Provenance-Oriented Baselines

Table IV complements the primary comparison in Table II with results for AgentArmor, TraceAegis, and ProvSEEK under the same AgentDojo evaluation settings.

Runtime-trace defenses suppress explicit execution deviations but remain sensitive to structurally plausible attack paths. As shown in Table IV, AgentArmor and TraceAegis reduce attack success more consistently when the injected objective induces a conspicuous change in the tool sequence or runtime behavior. Their remaining failures are concentrated primarily under Tool Knowledge, where injected procedural guidance can preserve valid tool names, arguments, and high-level control flow. This pattern is consistent with a limitation of trace-level enforcement: an execution path may remain structurally admissible even when the reason for selecting that path has shifted from the user objective to untrusted mediator content.

AgentArmor’s program-analysis constraints provide comparatively selective enforcement when an attack introduces an unsupported transition or violates an explicit execution invariant. However, such constraints cannot directly determine whether an otherwise valid transition is justified by the user task or merely suggested by injected tool documentation. TraceAegis exhibits a related limitation at the behavioral level. Legitimate multi-step workflows may contain uncommon branches, optional tool calls, and model-dependent planning choices, making it difficult for anomaly detection to distinguish malicious deviations from benign trajectory diversity. This ambiguity is consistent with its larger benign intervention cost.

Provenance evidence does not by itself establish whether a pending action is user-authorized. ProvSEEK reconstructs where execution evidence originates and how it propagates through the agent workflow. Such information is useful for forensic analysis, but benign and injected content may enter through the same authorized tool and therefore exhibit similar provenance structures. Provenance can identify the source of an artifact without determining whether the artifact’s influence on a pending action is consistent with the current user objective. The results in Table IV are consistent with this gap between provenance reconstruction and selective runtime mitigation: conservative treatment of untrusted provenance can remove task-relevant evidence, whereas permissive treatment can leave instruction-bearing influence in the execution state.

Appendix D Case Study: Tool-Knowledge Takeover in Travel

We next present a concrete AgentDojo case to illustrate how indirect prompt injection enters the live agent state and how AgentSentry restores the intended workflow through boundary-local replay attribution and purified continuation. All outcomes in this section refer to the same Travel/user_task_6/injection_task_6 instance with Qwen3-Max.

The selected case is challenging because the observable tool sequence remains consistent with the benign hotel-planning task, while the injected objective is realized only in the final natural-language response. This case is illustrative rather than an estimate of failure frequency; quantitative conclusions are based on the aggregate results in Table II.

Appendix E Mechanism-Targeted Adaptive Stress Grid

The black-box studies use Qwen3-Max at temperature 00 with (w,δL,δM,γ)=(3,0,0,0.25)(w,\delta_{L},\delta_{M},\gamma)=(3,0,0,0.25). Each protocol retains its own denominator, and transformations whose same-case undefended control does not produce the attacker-specified action are not credited as defense successes.

The adaptive grid contains 36 attack transformations and 36 structure-matched benign controls, each instantiated at L∈{6,12}L\in\{6,12\} and three trigger positions while preserving the user goal, host record, attack objective, and effect-bearing tool signature. The conditions target distinct components of the pipeline: trigger-position adaptation stresses the sliding window, cross-return retrieval stresses grounded evidence assembly, probe-aware masking evasion stresses the probe contract, and factual-recipient poisoning stresses the assumption that effect-bearing values are instruction-bearing.

For each attack, a side-effect-free same-case undefended execution determines whether the attacker-specified pending action is produced at all; conditional metrics use the resulting frozen set of 19 activated attacks. The defended runner is also side-effect-free, so “attack survival” denotes an unsafe pending action that survives diagnosis rather than an externally committed effect.

AgentSentry prevents 17 of the 19 activated unsafe pending actions, giving a conditional survival rate of 10.53%10.53\% with an exact 95%95\% Clopper–Pearson interval of [1.30%,33.14%][1.30\%,33.14\%]. It raises an alarm in 18 of 19 cases and localizes 17 of 19 within one boundary.

Every activated instruction-bearing transformation is blocked, and each condition is informative about a different component. Relocating the trigger does not help the attacker because the local gate is referenced to the pending proposal rather than to a fixed offset from the injection: moving the trigger changes which boundary raises the alarm, not whether one is raised. Cross-return retrieval is localized exactly in only 2 of 5 cases, since the attack becomes identifiable only once enough fragments have entered the state to be associated with a common source set; the remaining three are still localized within one boundary, so the cost is a bounded lag rather than diffuse attribution. Three probe-aware constructions do not activate at all, because the obfuscation needed to evade the audit contract also weakens the directive enough that the undefended policy stops adopting it.

Both survivors are factual-recipient-poisoning cases, which lie outside the operator’s scope by construction. The mediator supplies the recipient as plausible factual metadata, so no span satisfies the control-evidence contract of Section IV-C, purification reduces to the identity, and both SbMS_{b}^{M} and SbLS_{b}^{L} remain zero. Replay establishes dependence on removable control content; it does not adjudicate the truth of a plausible field value. The three prevented cases in this condition are those where the poisoned value retains procedural framing that the audit recovers.

Persistent-memory and provenance-spoofing transformations do not activate, 0 of 6 in each condition, and are not credited as successes. Because the grid uses correlated transformations of a small number of seeds, it is a targeted stress test rather than an i.i.d. sample.
